headline: 8 arrested in Mohammadpur over kidnapping; RAB identifies one as Patali Group leader
summary: Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) has apprehended eight suspects suspects in connection with a kidnapping case in Dhaka's Mohammadpur area.
details: The Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) has arrested eight individuals in Mohammadpur, Dhaka, in connection with a kidnapping case.
Among the detainees, RAB has identified one person as the leader of the so-called 'Patali Group'.
The arrests were carried out as part of an ongoing investigation into the kidnapping incident in the area.
The suspects are now under interrogation to uncover more details about the kidnapping operation and other potential crimes.

headline_marked: 2.4 crore children target: [[Govt launches nationwide Vitamin A Plus campaign]]
headline: 2.4 crore children target: Govt launches nationwide Vitamin A Plus campaign
summary: The drive aims to provide vitamin A capsules to children aged six months to under five years across 1.2 lakh centres.
details: The government has launched a nationwide Vitamin A Plus campaign to provide vitamin A capsules to 2.40 crore children aged between six months and under five years.
Health Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain inaugurated the campaign at the Shaheed Abu Sayed International Conference Center in Dhaka.
The campaign is being conducted through approximately 1.20 lakh centres and 500 mobile centres across the country, operating from 8:00 am to 4:00 pm.
This initiative follows a measles-rubella vaccination campaign conducted in April and May, which targeted 1.82 crore children in the same age group.
While the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) reported achieving 103 percent of the measles-rubella target, public health experts have raised concerns.
Experts point to a large discrepancy in the target population figures between the two campaigns, suggesting weaknesses in population data planning.
This data gap is particularly concerning as Bangladesh continues to report around 1,000 new measles infections daily, despite the government's claims of exceeding vaccination targets.
caption:
2.4 crore children are the target of the government's new nationwide Vitamin A Plus campaign.

The government has launched a nationwide Vitamin A Plus campaign to provide vitamin A capsules to 2.40 crore children aged between six months and under five years.

Health Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain inaugurated the campaign at the Shaheed Abu Sayed International Conference Center in Dhaka.

The campaign is being conducted through approximately 1.20 lakh centres and 500 mobile centres across the country, operating from 8:00 am to 4:00 pm.

This initiative follows a measles-rubella vaccination campaign conducted in April and May, which targeted 1.82 crore children in the same age group.

While the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) reported achieving 103 percent of the measles-rubella target, public health experts have raised concerns.

Experts point to a large discrepancy in the target population figures between the two campaigns, suggesting weaknesses in population data planning.

This data gap is particularly concerning as Bangladesh continues to report around 1,000 new measles infections daily, despite the government's claims of exceeding vaccination targets.
